prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of GLP-1 physiology and the active incretin peptide that made possible incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: B014 is the only candidate on which all six of us placed first, and I still think that reflects the science rather than momentum. The chain from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36) to drugs used by millions is unusually complete, independently confirmed by large randomized outcome trials, and has extended beyond glycaemia to cardiovascular, renal and weight outcomes. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue. A single-achievement prize with three people keeps the discovery narrative intact and avoids splitting a prize that does not need splitting.
statement.case_against: The attribution is the weak point. Any three names exclude a legitimate claimant: Knudsen for translation into liraglutide and semaglutide, Mojsov for identifying the active peptide form, and Habener and colleagues for early proglucagon work who are not on the list. There is also a real question of whether a prize that leans on industrial drug development sits comfortably beside basic physiology. If the committee decides that therapy must be rewarded explicitly, my trio becomes harder to defend.

responses.point: Perlmann favours Holst, Drucker and Mojsov and treats Knudsen's role as largely industrial drug development.
responses.response: I agree on the trio and reached it independently, but I would not call Knudsen's contribution merely industrial. Turning a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug was a creative scientific step and it is why patients benefit at all. My reason for preferring Mojsov is narrower: the prize citation can then rest on physiology and the identification of the active peptide, which are discoveries, and the committee is not forced to adjudicate between pharmaceutical programmes. I accept this is a judgement call, and I would not resist a Knudsen configuration strongly.

responses.point: Svenningsson proposes Drucker, Holst and Knudsen so that the prize spans mechanism through drug, noting Mojsov has a real but disputed claim.
responses.response: The mechanism-to-drug logic is attractive, and it is the best argument for the Knudsen version. My concern is that it leaves out the one person whose work defined the active GLP-1(7-36) form, and that omission carries a priority dispute into the citation. I would ask the chair to weigh whether the committee can document Mojsov's role well enough to defend inclusion, because if it cannot, I would move toward Knudsen rather than leave the third slot to a weaker claim.

responses.point: Linnarsson places B036 optogenetics second and B039 CAR-T third, and treats Knudsen as part of a coherent basic-to-translational trio for B014.
responses.response: I agree that B014 should be first, and I follow him in treating optogenetics as a serious candidate. But I rank it below the therapy candidates for two reasons: six credited names cannot be reduced to three without an arguable omission, and its clinical impact is still early. That contrasts with B039, where the credit problem is smaller and approved products exist. I would not rank B036 above B039 until the attribution is resolved.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks B003 second, calling Walter and Mori a clean two-person pairing with deep consequences for proteostasis and secretory physiology.
responses.response: I agree that attribution for B003 is the cleanest on the list, and it is why I keep it as an alternative. Where I qualify his view is clinical consequence: the concept is fundamental, but therapeutic exploitation is still preliminary. That makes it a strong prize in a year when the committee prefers a conceptual discovery, but it does not displace B014 and I would hesitate to pair it with B014, because that would require four names against a three-person limit.

uncertainties: Whether the evidence supports Mojsov or Knudsen as the third laureate for B014, and whether Habener's early proglucagon work changes the allocation.
Whether B039 should be two or three people, since Rosenberg's role is adjacent to the CAR design and clinical translation and early CAR originators are outside the credited list.
Whether the committee prefers a physiology-first citation or one that explicitly honours drug development for B014.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. I have co-authored with colleagues in KI single-cell genomics, but none of those collaborations concern the shortlisted discoveries or candidates.
